content: {"summary":"In February 2025 name resolution failed across auth, catalog and orders because CoreDNS pods were CPU‑starved with only two replicas, causing high latency and EAI_AGAIN errors; scaling to four replicas restored service.","likely_cause":"CPU starvation of CoreDNS due to insufficient replica count (2) under load","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"CoreDNS pods hit their CPU ceiling, causing request latency to rise to seconds.","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#1"],"quote":"2 replicas, each flat against its CPU ceiling"},{"text":"Scaling CoreDNS to four replicas reduced latency and restored name resolution.","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#1"],"quote":"scaled coredns to 4 replicas ... errors were fading and lookups came back clean"},{"text":"All namespaces lost resolution because they rely on CoreDNS, while VMs querying internal‑dns directly were unaffected.","evidence_ids":["INC-0016#2"],"quote":"Starve those CoreDNS pods of CPU and every namespace loses name resolution together"}],"next_checks":["Verify CoreDNS replica count and enable autoscaling","Monitor CoreDNS request p99 latency and CPU usage","Add alert on CoreDNS request p99 exceeding threshold","Review capacity planning for query volume spikes"]}
